A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Video-Panda. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the renumbered appendix sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original Video-Panda question-answering results, efficiency measurements, and architectural and training ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds results on EgoSchema and VideoMME-M, FLOP measurements and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The STAB architecture, spatial and temporal components, token construction, losses and three-stage training procedure are retained. No change to the proposed method is established.

E1.justification: New Appendix D and Table 11 substantially broaden evaluation coverage by adding EgoSchema and VideoMME-M as further long-video benchmarks. The existing QA benchmarks, fine-grained evaluation and training datasets remain.

E2.justification: ST-LLM is added to the different-training-data comparisons in Tables 1 and 2. Other comparator sets are retained; Table 11 extends comparisons with the existing Video-ChatGPT and Video-LLaVA baselines to the added benchmarks.

E3.justification: Table 3 adds FLOPs as an efficiency metric alongside parameters and latency. Existing sampling, preprocessing, training settings and QA metrics are unchanged. Separate procedures for the new long-video evaluations are not specified.

E4.justification: Figures 6–8 add twelve qualitative QA examples from MSRVTT-QA, TGIF-QA and ActivityNet-QA, illustrating capabilities including action recognition, counting and temporal understanding. Existing component, loss, downsampling and teacher ablation results are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Adds long-video accuracies in Table 11: Video-Panda 36.4/37.9, Video-ChatGPT 34.2/36.0 and Video-LLaVA 36.1/38.1 on EgoSchema/VideoMME-M. Also adds ST-LLM results, FLOP measurements and qualitative outputs. Existing tabulated scores remain unchanged, while Figure 1 corrects Video-LLaMA's plotted parameter count from approximately 1.4B to 1.1B.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations 1–20 retain the same attention operations, representations and training losses. Changes are limited to punctuation and typesetting; no theoretical result or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the encoder-free contribution, 45M visual parameters, competitive QA performance and 3–4× processing-speed claims. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly interprets the long-video results as confirming comparable accuracy with lower computational requirements. V1 only suggested potential benefits for longer videos in its conclusion. Existing mechanism explanations and qualifications are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: The advertised code link changes from a GitHub repository to a project webpage, and acknowledgements newly identify Leonardo/CINECA compute access. Table 10 specifies InternVideov2 instead of InternVideo, with unchanged scores; this does not establish an actual experiment change.

R1.justification: Adds a discussion of ST-LLM and references for ST-LLM, EgoSchema and Video-MME. The encoder-free research positioning remains substantively unchanged. Several other bibliography edits update publication metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: Includes limited copyediting, an affiliation update and a new acknowledgement section. Inserting Appendix D shifts the former Appendices D–F to E–G; the main exposition and section structure are largely retained.

P2.justification: Adds Table 11 and Figures 6–8, expands Tables 1–3, adjusts Figure 1 and clarifies Figure 5's caption. These are localized display changes; the existing architecture and ablation artwork and overall two-column layout remain.

improvement.justification: The added long-video evaluations, ST-LLM comparisons and FLOP measurements strengthen support for the existing accuracy and efficiency argument. Correcting Figure 1 also improves consistency. The gain is limited by sparse protocol documentation for the new benchmarks, while the main method and existing results remain unchanged.
